Accounts and payroll

Where the month actually went

Fee income on one side, salaries and rent and utilities on the other, and a profit figure that is the arithmetic of the two rather than somebody's estimate. No accounting training required to read it.

Start 14 day free trial See the handbook chapters

The expense ledger

Your own categories: salaries, rent, utilities, repairs, whatever your school spends on. A category can be retired but never deleted, because deleting one would orphan every old entry filed under it and change last year's figures.

Cash drawer sessions

A collector opens a drawer, takes fees, and closes it by counting what is there. A difference between the counted cash and the receipts is not rounded away: it is recorded with a written reason, which is the whole point of counting.

The day book

Everything that moved today, in one list, with who entered it. It is the screen a principal opens at six o'clock, and the one that makes a question about a particular receipt answerable in seconds.

Staff and payroll

Staff records, salaries, staff attendance with a daily check in code, and printable staff cards. Teacher logins are tied to the classes each teacher actually teaches, and a leaving date closes the login.

Two honest limits

Because finding out on a Monday morning is worse than reading it here.

  • This is not a general ledger. There is no double entry, no trial balance and no chart of accounts. It answers what came in, what went out and what is left, which is the question a school office actually has.
  • The statement is not a bank document. A printed account statement says so at the bottom, because a parent will one day take it to a bank and be turned away, and it is better that the paper says why.
